subject: math
title: Grade 3 Rounding and Estimating
seo_title: Grade 3 Rounding and Estimating Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Round whole numbers to the nearest ten or hundred, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on rounding and estimating, aligned to the Ontario curriculum (B1.3, B2.3): round to the nearest ten and hundred on number lines, use the 5 rule, estimate sums and differences, check if answers are reasonable and solve word problems. 100 questions with an answer key. key_big: Look one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. 450 rounds to 500.
key_sub: Estimate before you calculate: 386 + 247 is about 400 + 200 = 600. If your answer is far from the estimate, check your work.
body_html:
Rounding: find the closer ten or hundred

Rounding finds the closest ten or hundred. Rounded numbers are easy to add and subtract in your head.

The 5 rule

Look at the digit one place to the right of the place you are rounding to. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.

Round to the nearestLook at theExample
tenones digit365 → 370
hundredtens digit682 → 700
Exactly halfway

Round 450 to the nearest hundred.

450 is exactly halfway between 400 and 500. The tens digit is 5, and 5 rounds up.

Answer: 500

A 9 that rounds up

Round 960 to the nearest hundred.

The tens digit is 6, so round up. 9 hundreds and 1 more hundred make 10 hundreds.

Answer: 1000

Estimate, then check

An estimate is a quick answer that is close to the exact answer. Round the numbers, then add or subtract in your head. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, check your work.

Estimate a sum

About how many people? 386 adults and 247 children.

Round to the nearest hundred: 400 + 200 = 600. The exact answer is 633, which is close.

Answer: about 600

Estimate a difference

Estimate 812 − 385.

Round to the nearest hundred: 800 − 400 = 400. The exact answer is 427.

Answer: about 400

Is the answer reasonable?

Arjun says 604 − 278 = 474.

Estimate: 600 − 300 = 300. 474 is far from 300, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 326.

Answer: not reasonable

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding 450 down to 400Exactly halfway rounds up: 500
Looking at the wrong digit: 349 to the nearest hundred → 350For the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit: 4, so 300
Always rounding down: 682 → 600The tens digit is 8 (5 or more), so round up: 700
Rounding in two steps: 349 → 350 → 400Look only at the tens digit: 4, so 300
Not checking: 59 + 87 = 1316Estimate 60 + 90 = 150; 1316 is far too big. The answer is 146

faq.q: What does Grade 3 learn about rounding in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 3 students round whole numbers to the nearest ten or hundred in real situations (B1.3). They also use mental math and estimation to add and subtract numbers up to 1000 (B2.3).
To the nearest hundred, 450 rounds to 500. A number exactly halfway between two hundreds is rounded up.

faq.q: What is the difference between rounding and estimating?
faq.a: Rounding changes one number to the closest ten or hundred. Estimating uses rounded numbers to get a quick answer, such as 386 + 247 is about 400 + 200 = 600.

faq.q: How can my child check if an answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Estimate first by rounding, then compare. If 59 + 87 gives 1316 but 60 + 90 = 150, the answer is far too big and should be checked. This habit helps on the Grade 3 EQAO math assessment too.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 60 when you round to the nearest ten?
items.e: The numbers that round to 60 are 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63 and 64. 54 rounds down to 50. The smallest is 55, because a 5 in the ones place rounds up.

items.q: What is the largest whole number that rounds to 400 when you round to the nearest hundred?
items.e: Numbers from 350 to 449 round to 400. 450 is exactly halfway, so it rounds up to 500. 440 rounds to 400, but 449 is larger. The largest is 449.

items.q: Mei says 450 rounds to 400 when you round to the nearest hundred. Is she right?
items.e: 450 is exactly halfway between 400 and 500. The tens digit is 5, and 5 rounds up. Mei is not right: 450 rounds to 500.

items.q: Owen rounds 682 to the nearest hundred and gets 600. What should he get?
items.e: Owen always rounded down. Look at the tens digit: 8. 8 is 5 or more, so round up. 682 rounds to 700.

items.q: Zoe rounds 349 to the nearest hundred. She says “349 → 350 → 400.” What is the right answer?
items.e: Do not round in two steps. To round to the nearest hundred, look only at the tens digit: 4. 4 is 4 or less, so round down. 349 rounds to 300.
